featured_reviews.name: Dj FTB
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited this restaurant recently and had a really good dining experience. We tried the crab masala, surmai thali, mutton thali, chicken crispy, and soup. The crab masala was slightly on the expensive side, but the taste and quality made it worth trying. The surmai and mutton thalis were satisfying with good portions and authentic flavors. Chicken crispy was well cooked and flavorful, while the soup was comforting and tasty. Overall, the food was nice, service was good, and the experience was enjoyable.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are hunting for genuine, no-fuss Konkani and Malvani food in Mumbai, your search ends at Konkan Swad in Jogeshwari West. This restaurant is truly a hidden gem, offering an unparalleled taste of the coast that transports you straight to the shores of Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg. It's the kind of place you visit when you crave authentic, home-style seafood and fiery curries.
The highlight here is, without a doubt, the seafood. The fish is always incredibly fresh—a mandatory requirement for any great coastal establishment. I highly recommend starting with the Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck) or the Surmai Fry. The coating is perfectly crisp, and the marinade is a flawless blend of chili, turmeric, and spice. For the main course, the Prawn Curry Thali is a masterpiece; rich, coconut-based gravy that pairs perfectly with the soft, fluffy Vade (puri made from rice and lentil flour). If you prefer meat, the Chicken Malvani Thali is equally robust and satisfying.
Beyond the main courses, don't miss out on the incredible Solkadhi. This kokam-based digestive drink is creamy, tangy, and absolutely essential for cooling the palate after the spicy Konkani flavors. It’s one of the best I've had outside of a Konkani home.
The ambiance is simple, clean, and unpretentious, allowing the focus to remain solely on the food, as it should be. The staff is warm, helpful, and eager to offer recommendations, making the entire dining experience feel incredibly homely. If you love coastal flavors, fresh fish, and authentic Malvani spices, Konkan Swad is a must-visit destination in Jogeshwari. Highly, highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Sanntosh Shringarpure
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hits and misses at this Mangalorean spot:

​I visited The Fisherman’s Kitchen on a Friday evening with high expectations, given the name and the positive reviews. While the atmosphere is family-friendly and the location is convenient (right below Bangur Nagar Metro with valet parking), the food was a mixed bag.
​The Standouts: The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was easily the highlight—the fish was incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked (4.5/5). Pairing the remaining gravy with Neer Dosa was the best part of the meal.
​The Letdowns: Unfortunately, the Prawns Tandoori didn't taste fresh (2.5/5), and the Crab Soup was watery with very little meat. The Kadipatta Chicken was also quite average; the chicken felt a bit tough and lacked that punchy Mangalorean flavor I was looking for.
​The Verdict:
​Ambience & Service: 3.5/5
​Alcohol Variety: 4/5
Food: 3/5
​Value for Money: 3/5
It’s a decent place for a family outing, and perhaps I caught them on an off-night, but for a seafood specialty restaurant, I expected more consistency in freshness.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place has a G+2 seating arrangement—non-AC on the ground floor and AC seating on the first and second floors. Seating is decent.

Unlike many traditional bars, no complimentary chakna is served here. Alcohol prices felt on the higher side, and the 180 ml vodka was served from a larger container instead of a sealed bottle, which was a bit disappointing. Mixers were limited to Coke and Sprite only. Initially, staff said outside mixers would be charged extra, but after speaking to the manager, they allowed to buy it from outside without any charge.

Service was decent but not very attentive, especially towards regular or light drinkers—attention seemed more focused on heavy customers.

Coming to food: Apple Chicken was good, and the green kokani/malvani-style kairi chutney served with it was unique and delicious. We ordered Chicken Thali (₹300) and Mutton Thali (₹430). Quantity felt slightly less for the price—total four pieces (two gravy, two fry). Taste-wise, chicken and mutton gravies and fries had almost the same masala, which reduced variety.

Ambience is decent overall, but the washroom ceiling is quite low, which can be uncomfortable for tall people.

Overall, a decent experience—good chutney and some dishes stand out, but quantity, attention to service, and a few basic facilities can definitely improve.

The pomfret fry was absolutely bland, with no salt or spices—completely tasteless and frankly pathetic. The prawns masala was just okay, nothing special and far from what you’d expect from a place claiming coastal flavors. Mushroom chilli and rotis were average at best.
Overall, a regretful visit. The food quality and taste did not justify the long wait or the expectations set by the restaurant’s name. Definitely not worth it and would not recommend.

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Ali Baba Cafe, and it’s a great spot if you’re craving rich non-veg dishes, especially Mughlai and Middle Eastern-style cuisine.

The place is quite popular for its flavourful tandoori items, kebabs, and hearty gravies. We started with the Chicken Tawa Chilly, which had a nice spicy kick and was perfectly cooked. The Chicken Barra Tandoori was juicy, smoky, and full of flavour — definitely one of the highlights.

For the main course, we tried the Chicken Mandi Rice, which was aromatic and well-balanced, giving proper Middle Eastern vibes. The Mutton Galouti Kebab was super soft and melted in the mouth, while the Mutton Nihari was rich, slow-cooked, and full of deep flavours.

They also serve refreshing drinks like Sangria Champagne Bar, which added a nice touch to the meal. We ended with Gulab Jamun, which was warm, soft, and a perfect sweet finish.

Overall, the service and management were good and everything was served on time. If you’re a non-veg lover, this place definitely deserves to be on your list for a satisfying and flavour-packed meal.

I am extremely disappointed with my recent order from JP’s Lunch Home. I had ordered mutton gravy expecting a proper dish with meat, but what I received was just plain gravy with absolutely no mutton pieces in it.

This is not a minor mistake—the main component of the dish was completely missing. It feels misleading to charge customers for a mutton dish and deliver something that doesn’t even contain mutton.

What makes it worse is the inconvenience caused. I was left without a proper meal and had to go through the hassle of raising a complaint and following up for resolution. This is not the level of service one expects when ordering from a listed restaurant.

Restaurants need to take basic quality checks seriously before dispatching orders. Sending out incomplete items reflects very poorly on both the restaurant and the delivery platform.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and necessary action is taken so that other customers do not face the same issue.

This was not just bad service, this was outright insulting behavior by your staff.

This was extremely humiliating, especially in front of others. My wife felt insulted and we had to explicitly ask him to stay away from our table.
Let me be very clear, this is not a small mistake. This reflects complete failure in staff training, customer respect and management oversight.
We chose not to create a scene there, but this experience has ensured we will never return.
If this is the standard of service you tolerate, customers should think twice before visiting.
Train your staff or replace them because this level of behavior is unacceptable.

featured_reviews.name: Avalon John
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last weekend, I had the pleasure of dining at a delightful local restaurant that truly exceeded my expectations. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with warm smiles and genuine hospitality. The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive without being overbearing, which immediately set a welcoming tone for the evening.

The restaurant itself was neat, well-organized, and spotless—a rare and refreshing sight these days. Tables were clean, the atmosphere was cozy, and even the washrooms were well-maintained.

I ordered the mutton biryani and a lime soda, and both were absolutely spot-on. The biryani was aromatic and flavorful, with tender chunks of mutton that fell apart effortlessly. The spices were perfectly balanced—not too overpowering, but enough to leave a lasting impression. The lime soda was refreshing, tangy, and the perfect companion to the rich biryani.

What really stood out, aside from the great food, was how reasonably priced everything was. It's hard to find such quality and cleanliness at such affordable rates these days. Overall, this place is a gem for anyone looking for tasty food, a clean setting, and top-notch service without breaking the bank. I’ll definitely be coming back—and bringing friends along next time.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely terrible experience and one of the worst examples of customer service I have come across.

We waited nearly 40–50 minutes for our food, only to receive an order that was completely different from what we had actually ordered. When this was brought to the staff’s attention, instead of apologizing or taking responsibility, we were told that the staff member was inexperienced. How is that the customer’s problem? If your staff is not properly trained, customers should not have to suffer because of it.

The AC was not working at all, making the dining experience extremely uncomfortable. When we complained, the response was essentially, It is what it is. No solution, no concern, no effort to help.

The level of mismanagement became even more apparent during billing. The items mentioned on the bill were different from the items we had actually received, but casually said it was fine because the total amount matched. Imagine a restaurant openly admitting that the bill does not match the order and expecting customers to accept it as normal.

The most shocking part came at the end. After serving the wrong order, making us wait almost an hour, and showing zero accountability throughout the experience, we were asked, “If it was wrong, then why did you eat it?” This statement perfectly sums up the attitude of the restaurant. Instead of acknowledging their mistakes, they chose to blame the customer.

No accountability, no professionalism, poor service, poor management, and complete disregard for customer experience. Mistakes can happen, but the arrogance and refusal to take responsibility are what make this place stand out for all the wrong reasons.

I would strongly advise others to think twice before dining here.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Something’s Fishy last week to celebrate a family friend’s birthday.

If you’re a seafood lover, Something’s Fishy is the kind of place that instantly feels right. From the moment you step in, the ambience sets the mood. The interiors have a beautiful seafood-inspired theme, artistically done without being over the top. Subtle marine elements, thoughtful décor, and warm lighting make the space feel relaxed and inviting. It’s comfortable enough for a family dinner yet stylish enough for a special outing.

We tried quite a variety of dishes, and honestly, the experience from start to finish was satisfying.

Harra Channa ka Shorba (Chicken Soup): A comforting, mildly spiced chicken soup with fresh herb flavours. Light yet flavourful, it had a soothing warmth and well-balanced seasoning, perfect to begin the meal.

Chicken Gassi: Rich, coastal-style chicken curry with aromatic spices and creamy coconut base. The gravy was flavourful without being overpowering, and the chicken pieces were tender and well-cooked.

Appams: Soft, fluffy appams with delicate crisp edges. Light texture and subtle sweetness paired beautifully with the gassi gravies, soaking up flavours perfectly without becoming soggy.

Prawn Gassi: Fresh prawns cooked in traditional coastal gravy with coconut and spices. The prawns were juicy and tender, absorbing the rich masala while retaining their natural sweetness.

Butter Garlic Prawn: Perfectly sautéed prawns tossed in butter and garlic. Simple yet delicious, with a lovely aroma and balanced seasoning that allowed the freshness of the seafood to shine.

Surmai Fry: Crispy on the outside, moist and flaky inside. The fish was fresh, well-marinated, and fried just right, delivering bold coastal flavours without excessive oiliness.

Rawas Tandoori: Well-marinated rawas grilled to perfection in the tandoor. Smoky, juicy, and packed with spices, yet the fish remained soft and flavourful inside.

Squid Crispy Fried Rings: Lightly battered squid rings fried till crisp. Crunchy outside, tender inside, with balanced seasoning that made them addictive without feeling too heavy.

What stood out throughout the meal was the freshness of the seafood. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, not rushed. Portions were generous, and the flavours felt authentic rather than overly commercialised.

Service was smooth and friendly. The staff were attentive, happy to recommend dishes, and ensured everything was served at the right pace. They didn’t hover unnecessarily, which made the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, Something’s Fishy delivers exactly what you expect from a seafood speciality restaurant — fresh ingredients, authentic coastal flavours, and a warm, pleasant ambience. It’s definitely a place I’d revisit whenever seafood cravings strike. Highly recommended for anyone who truly enjoys well-prepared seafood.

featured_reviews.name: Jyothis Thaliath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for lunch.  It’s a Marathi-style seafood speciality restaurant that promises authentic coastal flavours.

Ambience:
The outdoor dining area has a lovely rustic vibe, perfect for evenings or cooler days. However, during hot afternoons, it can get quite uncomfortable. There’s also an indoor, air-conditioned section, but the tables are tightly packed and the sofa type seating is bit aged and not very comfortable.

Food:
We tried two thalis — Mutton Thali and Surmai Thali.

The Mutton Thali was the highlight of our meal. The mutton chops were tender, perfectly spiced, and among the best I’ve had in a while. The gravy was rich and flavourful without being overpowering. The marrow-filled bone was a pleasant surprise.

The Surmai Thali, on the other hand, was average. The fish fry portion was large but just okay in taste.

I wouldn’t recommend the Thalis here overall as most of the side dishes were quite oily and didn’t match my palate (though Maharashtrians might enjoy that style).

Thalis are priced on the higher side (₹600–₹1200). While portions are generous enough to share, I’d suggest skipping the Thali and focusing on starters or individual seafood dishes for better value and taste.

We also tried Butter Garlic Prawns, which were disappointing. Also, the prawns added into Thali curries felt out of place. They could consider swapping a few prawn dishes for clams or calamari, which are common in  Malvani cuisine.

Overall:
Don't fall for the social media hype. It's good for a visit if you’re in Aarey and craving for seafood.

featured_reviews.name: Dipen Rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went here for dinner today.
Ordered
Prawns Butter Garlic
Squid Rings / Deep Fry
Prawns Malwani Curry
Neer Dosa
Surmai Thali

All the food items were good except the Surmai Fry in the thali was having a bad odour. we had to leave the half portion of the fish as we could have it due to the odour.

We were served with a bowl of peanut to much on with beer.. After picking up couple of peanuts... we found a long piece of hair in it... we asked them to change the bowl.. the waiter took it back and return with the same bowl after shuffling the peanuts.

Was very impressed with their SolKadhi, Caramel Custard. and the way Javla was cooked.

featured_reviews.name: Nitesh Marchande
featured_reviews.review_text: Visit this place on Saturday 3rd Sept with family, superb ambience, service and staff good, delicious food (specially tandoori was well cooked) also we ordered 1 Pomfret thali and 1 prawns thali both are yummy.we will revisit very soon.

featured_reviews.name: sujata shetty
featured_reviews.review_text: We had heard such great things about food at Machhli that we had to to try it and so glad that we did! I went with family there and I tried their crab thali which was reallyyyyy good. My other family members tried their fish and mutton thali which they loved as well. This place has some great kids menu too and my daughter who is very picky eater finished all the food we had ordered for her. Also how can I not mention their superb dessert collection, I still remember the yummy taste of the Chikku halwa and rose petal ice-cream. In all, this place was totally worth our visit and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for good quality and delicious food!!

featured_reviews.review_text: I tried surmai and pomfret thali taste was amazing if you love sea food then you should must try surmai thali but the price of the thali is high and the size of the fish was small the ambience is good overall great place must visit For sea food
